Build the conditional transition probability matrix of an HSMM

tpm_switch.Rd

Hidden semi-Markov models are defined in terms of state dwell times and conditional transition probabilities, given that the current state is left. These form the matrix \(\Omega\) (omega), also called the embedded transition probability matrix, whose diagonal entries are zero as self-transitions are impossible.

This function builds \(\Omega\) from unconstrained parameters, applying the inverse multinomial logistic link (softmax) to each row. With a design matrix Z, it builds one matrix for each row of Z, so that \(\Omega\) depends on covariates. Compatible with automatic differentiation by RTMB.

Usage

tpm_switch(beta = NULL, Z = NULL, byrow = FALSE, report = TRUE)

Arguments

beta

parameters; either

  • NULL (default) for 2 states, which have no free parameters,

  • a vector of length nStates * (nStates - 2), or

  • a matrix of dimension c(nStates * (nStates - 2), p + 1) if Z is provided, with the intercepts in the first column.

Z

optional covariate design matrix with or without intercept column, i.e. of dimension c(nObs, p) or c(nObs, p + 1). If it has p columns, a column of ones is added.

byrow

logical; if TRUE, the parameters of each row of the matrix are consecutive, see ‘Details’. Defaults to FALSE.

report

logical; if TRUE (default), the coefficient matrix beta is reported from the fitted model, if Z is provided.

Value

conditional transition probability matrix of dimension c(nStates, nStates), or array of such matrices of dimension c(nStates, nStates, nObs) if Z is provided

Details

Each row has nStates - 1 off-diagonal entries, of which the first is the reference (its predictor is fixed to 0), so there are nStates * (nStates - 2) free parameters: none for 2 states, 3 for 3 states, 8 for 4 states. The parameters fill a matrix with one row per state and nStates - 2 columns, whose row i holds the parameters of the second, third, ... off-diagonal entry of row i. By default, this matrix is filled by column, so that the parameters of row i are i, i + nStates, ... (as in tpm_emb() of earlier versions). With byrow = TRUE, it is filled by row, so that the parameters of each row are consecutive. With Z, the rows of beta are in the same order.

See also

Other transition probability matrix functions: generator(), generator_g(), tpm(), tpm_ct(), tpm_g(), tpm_g2(), tpm_p()

Examples

# 2 states: no free parameters
omega <- tpm_switch()

# 3 states: 3 free parameters
omega <- tpm_switch(c(0.5, -0.2, 0.1))

# 4 states: 8 free parameters
omega <- tpm_switch(rep(0, 8))

# 3 states, depending on a covariate
z <- rnorm(100)
beta <- cbind(c(0.5, -0.2, 0.1), c(0.3, 0, -0.4)) # intercepts and slopes
omega <- tpm_switch(beta, cbind(1, z)) # array with 100 slices

# 4 states, with the parameters of each row one after another
omega <- tpm_switch(c(0.5, -1, 0.2, 0, 0.3, -0.4, 1, -0.1), byrow = TRUE)
